source_name: ClassNK Register of Ships (Reg No. 162819) / Oshima Shipbuilding Co., Ltd. (Hull 10793 Technical Specification)
notes: Evidence Breakdown & CSR Derivation Investigation: (1) Directly Inspected Statutory Record: ClassNK Register of Ships Reg No. 162819 directly confirms IMO 9766944, Oshima Hull 10793, delivery 2016-09-02, DWT 82,103 MT, scantling draft 14.45 m, MAN B&W 6S60ME-C8.2, MCR 9,660 kW at 89.0 rpm. (2) Secondary Source-Reported Shipyard Specification: Oshima 82k Kamsarmax technical delivery sheet reports Lightweight Tonnage (LDT) 13,200 MT, laden scantling displacement 95,303 MT (82,103 + 13,200 MT), design speed 14.2 knots at Continuous Service Rating (CSR) 8,210 kW brake power. (3) CSR Provenance and Derivation Investigation: Reported CSR 8,210 kW corresponds to 84.990% (8210 / 9660 ≈ 84.9896%) of verified statutory MCR (9,660 kW * 0.85 = 8,211 kW, rounded to nearest 10 kW = 8,210 kW). In shipbuilding contract practice, Continuous Service Rating is conventionally contracted as a round figure or nominal 85% MCR rating with a 15% sea margin. Because ClassNK statutory registers do not publish CSR and original shipyard sea-trial test sheets are proprietary and inaccessible in public archives, whether 8,210 kW represents an independently measured trial power or a nominal 85% rule-of-thumb derivation cannot be independently verified. The value is retained as SOURCE_REPORTED, its derivation is classified as UNVERIFIED_SECONDARY_RELATIONSHIP, and the existing research-only restriction is preserved without recalculation. (4) Power Definition: Benchmark power is explicitly Continuous Service Rating engine brake power (P_B,CSR), NOT delivered shaft power (P_S) or trial measured power (P_trial). Calculated power output represents estimated required engine brake power at the flywheel coupling. (5) Model Limitations: Single-point calibration C_adm = (95303^(2/3) * 14.2^3) / 8210 = 727.37 is a first-order research approximation, NOT an independent validation of the full speed-power curve. The model evaluates strictly within the continuous rated-power boundary (<= 100% MCR). Ballast hydrostatics are unindexed; fails closed to UNAVAILABLE.
